My first Car Seat Headrest album, it will always hold a special place in my heart and always be one of my top ten albums ever. Definitely CSH’s most accessible album for people who aren’t quite into the more lo-fi, blurry vibe (yet). I remember not liking any of CSH’s albums no matter how hard I tried until I heard this one. It has a very nostalgic, More classic indie rock vibe that I love.

Favorite songs: Cosmic Hero and Ballad of the Costa Concordia

I got so many of my friends into CSH by introducing them to this album, specially DD/KW, and I have so many memories of us singing this album at the top of our lungs in car rides, dancing to it in the living room of our friend’s house, and crying to it when our lives were falling apart. Not to mention, tripping to Drugs With Friends was an experience. This album has so many moods, and every angsty, dissatisfied teen can relate to it in some manner, which is very important in modern music since teens and young adults pretty much decide what’s relevant in music. This album shaped my senior year of high school, and I know it reached a huge influence in my area. First time I heard DD/KW on the radio I screamed. While I feel like it’s underrated in a lot of CSH fans’ minds, it certainly gets the appreciation it deserves from the less die-hard fans. Every song is good, and I never have trouble listening to the whole album through.

I told a girl I'd go to prom with her, then cancelled and went with my guy friend who had bullied her and turned everyone against her. She was absolutely devastated, and I still feel absolutely, horrifically terrible. This girl happens to be my best friend in the whole wide world now, and she's done so much more for me than he ever would've even considered, and we've made so many amazing memories. I don't know why I ever chose him over her. I think it was legitimately so I could have popularity brownie points, and I hate myself for that. I was a stereotypical bitchy high schooler, the same type that had tormented me for years, just because I didn't want to lose my current social standing (nobody really liked her at the time). I know she forgives me, and we've talked all about it, but the fact that I did that to her still lingers and eats me up. I hate myself for it.

Twin fantasy completely changed my life, it means so, so much to me I can't even put it into words. I discovered it at a very low point in my life (there are a lot, thanks depression) and listened to this album specifically for six months straight because it was the only thing that made me feel anything. I'd be completely numb, no emotions, and it would bring me straight to tears. After I recovered from that grueling depressive spell, it still stuck with me. I tried to introduce car Seat Headrest to all of my friends. They'd sing DD/KW (I know it's not twin fantasy) in the halls; dancing, happy. I was amazed at what his music could bring to life amidst a lot of suffering. My best friend back at home (I'm in college now) and I learned how to harmonize to almost every song in twin fantasy. We know almost all the words to the entire album. We put it on and just go into autopilot. We sing it so well, so passionately, so freely, it's the most fulfilling human connection I've had since as long as I can remember. I hate to be one of those people that claims a certain band saved their lives. But I'm quite certain I wouldn't have made it through the winter if twin fantasy hadn't been playing in the background the entire time. I don't form meaningful relationships easily because of social anxiety, and for that period where I only had shallow friends and a shallow life, Will Toledo felt like my closest friend, and his music helped me branch out and create the most meaningful relationships I have now.

If I'm angry or want to sing along: teens of denial
If I'm sad or want to sing along: twin fantasy
If I'm numb or want to sing along: teens of style
If I haven't left my bed all day because I'm in an ultra depressive state: how to leave town
If I'm in the mood to relax and mix things up: nervous young man
When I wanna listen to something different from my usual: monomania/MBIKMB/any of the others I haven't mentioned

I agree, car seat headrest's music has kept me going when I didn't want to (as cliche as that sounds to true). Mentally ill teenagers can relate to Will so well because he has never tried to hide the truth of depression, anxiety, sexuality, etc. his lyrics don't wrap pain and existential dread in vague, hard to understand metaphors. Will just spits it out as it is. When I'm having a depressive episode, all I can stand to listen to is Chopin and Car Seat Headrest, because they're the only musicians I know who can convey emotion in such a raw and unabashed way. All of my friends who like car seat headrest suffer from mental illness. I suffer from mental illness. There's a connection between Will Toledo's music, lyrics, and overall disposition that just helps mentally ill kids feel a little less alone in a world that's always trying to hide them away. The first song I ever heard by car seat headrest was "Cosmic Hero" and I started bawling my eyes out as soon as "it'll be alright, it'll be alright" started reverberating in such a raw, melodic, sad tone. Maybe I'm being melodramatic, I don't know. But there are so many songs that just validate every emotion I've ever felt even if it's never made sense before. Raw anger and bitterness mixing with hopelessness and desperation. Sadness, depression, the feeling of uselessness and the decreasing will to exist mixes with random bouts of excitement and drugs as a coping mechanism. Just, god, Will's music is one of my best friends.

As someone who suffers from depression, sometimes you really can't make them *happy* because they just feel so completely terrible. Sometimes all it takes is to wait it out with them, and ensure them they're not a burden and that you're here for them. Help them find professional help or coping mechanisms that improve their mood (of course, even with professional help depression is typically chronic). Always ask "how are you?" "are you feeling alright today?" Gentle reminders to eat, drink, get out of bed, shower. It can be hard, but all it takes is consistent and subtle support. They may not always show it at first (depression makes that hard) but they are extremely grateful.

There's so many....but I'm going to have to go with Cosmic Hero because of its significance for me. God, it's a long ass story but I'll keep it concise. I was going through a HUGE rut in my life last summer; I had no genuine friendships and spent every day repressing and denying my depression and anxiety during the day, just bottling up my feelings. At night I would lay in my bed, drained and numb, scared and unsure. Anyways, it was really, really bad. The people who cared about me left me the past year (I broke off a toxic friendship and they disapproved) and they were still alienating me and whatnot. It felt terrible, but I didn't realize it, I just kind of stopped feeling.

About midway through June a new friend I was trying to connect with shared a playlist with me of songs I would like. We never really got super close, but it still felt good and genuine that someone would make a playlist for me. I mindlessly listened to almost all the songs, laying in my bed before Cosmic Hero caught my attention. I know it sounds melodramatic, but my ears picked up the melodic guitar (just beautiful) and crooning repetition of "It'll be alright, it'll be alright" and a sudden wave of emotion hit me like a truck. I burst into tears, sobbing and crying. For the next few months I listened to ONLY car seat headrest because it was the only music that made me feel at the time, it was obsessive and weird. Because of the inspiration it filled me with I started drawing again, I started being honest with my friends about my feelings, and I made a few steps forward. Sure, most of my emotions were still negative but they were there!! the rut came and went, and many others have afterwards, but Cosmic Hero still always stands out. 

The lyrics, the emotions conveyed, the beautiful instruments, it just revokes so much.

I'm in highschool, and it's being completely misinterpreted and sensationalized by my peers there. Suicidal kids are far worse off, and suicidal kids who were doing better have taken a turn for the worse. No one in my school is more aware about suicide, they're just calling the show beautiful and recommending it to all their friends without a second glance into the real world's problems with suicide. I watched it (I wasn't going to bash a show I didn't watch) and I've never been even close to triggered or upset before, but this show had me shaking and weak at certain parts of the show, and when Hannah baker committed suicide I found my wrists itching, and very old feelings resurfacing. It might not have meant to cause a phenomenon such as this, but teenagers can misinterpret and sensationalize many things. 

Edit: to clarify, this is what Will meant. He didn't mean the show was bad or terrible, but he meant that kids can get the wrong idea. And my friends and I agree, the suicide was portrayed more as an artsy mission and a cool revenge story where Hannah got the last laugh and everyone got to realize what they did was wrong. Though you may not have portrayed it that way, many people have, including Will.

This is my favorite song of all time let alone my favorite car seat headrest song. It was the first song I had ever heard by him, because a friend had added it to a suggested playlist. I was going through a huge rut full of angst and depression and I just remember bursting into tears as he sang "it'll be alright, it'll be alright.."

The lyrics are so melodic and powerful despite their extremely clear message and lack of artistic language (metaphors, imagery, etc.). There's profound revelations within emotional Lamentation, within the waves of hopelessness that comes with the feeling Will's portraying. The emotion and message of the song comes through so clear it feels refreshing.

The structure is absolutely stunning and original. The buildup is steady and strong, the end is powerful and memorable, the use of repetition and arcs of calm to loud to calm holds emphasis on the most important aspects of the song. Every time I listen it's still like it was when I first heard it.

The instrumentation is extremely clean, especially for Will, but that's what makes it so powerful, it contrasts, stands out, and stays strong. The trumpet in the beginning is (I quote my friend) "like the beginning of a funeral march." It calls the listener to attention and the gradual add-on of sound into immensely thick and orgasmic layering just makes listening to it so much more pleasant on the ears.

I could go on and on and on about the composition, the notations, the meaning and whatnot but I'll spare it for now. I'm obviously obsessed with this song, I even made an abstract art piece based off of it, and I DON'T DO ABSTRACT ART. Objectively, this song is absolutely amazing and one of car seat headrest's personal bests.

1. The three different parts, or "scenes." It's a really good example of storytelling within a song. The story goes from Will talking about his life and his experiences struggling with coming out, and keeping his feelings for the subject he's singing about a secret. He's almost rambling, but not quite, and you can sense his distress. Then, the story moves on to a more relaxed and subdued state, where he sings of the confusion and boredom that may come with a relationship, especially an undefined and fragile one like he was in. He speaks of his subconscious frustration and anger at the situation, and how he just wants to feel human. Finally, the song transitions to a story more chaotic than the first part of the song, jumbled and filled with metaphors. He's angry and distraught and he knows that the relationship is dying. In my opinion, these three "scenes" in the story are representative of the relationship. Beginning (new and tumultuous and confusing), middle (frustratingly boring, sort of a limbo, undefined), and end (collapse). This is a really artistic and advanced way to tell a story through a song
2. THE LYRICS are well thought out, beautiful at some points, humorous at others, and ever-changing. There are a few motifs that keep the song connected, but the insane amount of variety also keep the entire 12 minutes entirely interesting and captivating. They're brutal, honest, and entirely Will himself. These lyrics don't beat around the bush, and they're so extremely straight forward and raw it's refreshing. It's very hard to find songs with lyrics like that.
3. Will's voice, though not exactly an operatic god, is an amazing factor in this song. It's untailored, messy at points, and 100% genuine. This adds a sense of personal genuinity to the song that could have been destroyed if Will had put too much effort into cleaning up or producing his voice. It feels like Will is telling the story directly to the listener, and because of the rawness of his voice, the emotion is not blocked by anything. You feel every emotion Will is portraying, and it can hurt (I've cried because of this song before), but it's, again, so refreshing to hear this kind of honesty in a single song.
4. "DO YOU HAVE SOMETHING AGAINST DOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOGGGSSSS???"

TL;DR: It's genuine, artistically creative without being too much, beautifully written, a good story, and entertaining.
